closure.findingSummary: Removing a constituent queue item from a failed multi-volume extraction group left the failed group referencing the deleted item; retry then failed permanently with source_unavailable.

repairEvidence.detail: Removal still rejects queued/extracting groups. Removing an item now removes any non-complete extraction group that references it, queues its secret for cleanup, persists state, and attempts cleanup. Completed groups instead have only the removed item ID pruned; empty groups are dropped.

Rows belonging to queued/extracting extraction jobs are treated as active, suppressing the remove action. Other linked rows expose the localized accessible label/title that says removal cancels extraction while preserving downloaded files.
The removal label explicitly says 'cancel extraction, keep files' in English, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese.

The regression test removes one part from a failed two-volume group and asserts the remaining downloaded item is still complete, the extraction group is removed, the group secret is forgotten, and no extraction starts.

closure.assessment: The previously reported dangling-group retry path is closed in the pinned source. Removal cancels the whole non-terminal extraction group rather than leaving a partial, misleading retry group; native secret cleanup is attempted and persisted for later retry if unavailable. Completed groups are pruned without cancelling their completed result. No new finding was opened; this pass was limited to closure and directly affected synchronization/UI/password-cleanup behavior.
